evidence: Turner explicitly lists Sindhi gharavāro husband and Hindi gharwālā householder/husband, gharwālī wife under *gharapāla house-guardian. These complete survey formations preserve both the house base and the vāl-/vāḷ- member, with gender and local gh/k/b/w correspondences retained. The link is to the already analysed historical compound, not a partial house-only etymology; heavily contracted gharālā/kɛrɛlā and mixed responses are excluded.

Turner gives Punjabi sāī̃, Hindi sā̃ī and Maithili saĩẽ husband under svāmin, via Middle Indo-Aryan sāmi/sāhi. These nasalized survey sãi/sāhi forms fit that documented husband term; final -ek is retained as ordinary survey-context morphology. Less diagnostic sāhek and learned-looking swāmi forms are excluded.

Turner explicitly records Marathi navrā/naurā bridegroom or marriageable young man from *navavaraka newly wed. These western survey husband words extend the same spouse term beyond the wedding, preserving their vocalic forms.

Turner gives Hindi/Bihari/Awadhi bhatār husband from bhartṛ through Middle Indo-Aryan bhattāra. The survey bhatāras has this complete stem plus its recorded final inflection; it is not treated as a learned Sanskrit citation form.
